function.name: user_lock
function.description: This function locks the user mutex and, if it's the first lock, assigns the current thread ID to the user lock thread.
function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything

function.name: user_unlock
function.description: This function unlocks a user by decrementing the user_lock_rec and setting user_lock_thread to 0 if user_lock_rec reaches 0. It also unlocks a previously locked pthread_mutex.

parameters.name: void
parameters.description: This function does not take any parameters

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value

function.name: user_check_not_lock
function.description: This function checks if the current thread is the user lock thread. If it is, it logs an error and asserts false.

parameters.name: void
parameters.description: This function does not accept any parameters

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything

function.name: get_display_device_init_mutex
function.description: This function initializes a mutex for the display device. It creates a named mutex object, waits for the mutex to be signaled, and then returns the handle to the mutex.
function.return_type: HANDLE, which represents a handle to the mutex object. If the function fails, it returns 0.

function.name: release_display_device_init_mutex
function.description: This function releases a mutex and then closes the handle to it.

parameters.name: mutex
parameters.description: This is a handle to the mutex that needs to be released and closed.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: gpu_acquire
function.description: This function increments the reference count of the gpu structure and returns the same structure.

parameters.name: gpu
parameters.description: This parameter is a pointer to the gpu structure whose reference count is to be incremented.

function.return_type: struct gpu *; It represents the same gpu structure passed as parameter after incrementing its reference count.

function.name: gpu_release
function.description: This function decreases the reference count of the gpu object. If the reference count reaches zero, it frees the memory allocated to the gpu object.

parameters.name: gpu
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the gpu object whose reference count is to be decremented.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: source_acquire
function.description: This function increments the reference count of the source object and returns the same source object.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the source object whose reference count is to be incremented.

function.return_type: struct source *; Returns the same source object after incrementing its reference count.

function.name: source_release
function.description: This function decreases the reference count of the source object. If the reference count reaches zero, it releases the resources associated with the source object.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the source object whose reference count is to be decreased and resources are to be released if the reference count reaches zero.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value

function.name: monitor_release
function.description: This function decreases the reference count of a monitor object. If the reference count reaches zero, it releases the source of the monitor and frees the memory allocated for the monitor.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the monitor object whose reference count is to be decremented.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything

function.name: get_monitor_info_from_edid
function.description: This function extracts monitor information from the Extended Display Identification Data (EDID) and stores it in the provided info structure.

parameters.name: info
parameters.description: A pointer to a structure where the extracted monitor information will be stored.

parameters.name: edid
parameters.description: A pointer to the EDID data from which the monitor information will be extracted.

parameters.name: edid_len
parameters.description: The length of the EDID data.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value but modifies the info structure passed as a parameter.

function.name: debugstr_devmodew
function.description: This function generates a debug string for a DEVMODEW structure, providing information about the display mode settings.

parameters.name: devmode
parameters.description: Pointer to a DEVMODEW structure that contains information about the initialized display device.

function.return_type: char: Returns a string that represents the debug information of the display mode settings.

function.name: devmode_get
function.description: This function retrieves the value of a specified field from a DEVMODEW structure.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Pointer to a DEVMODEW structure from which the function retrieves the value.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: Specifies the field whose value is to be retrieved. This parameter can be one of the following values: DM_DISPLAYORIENTATION, DM_BITSPERPEL, DM_PELSWIDTH, DM_PELSHEIGHT, DM_DISPLAYFLAGS, DM_DISPLAYFREQUENCY, DM_DISPLAYFIXEDOUTPUT.

function.return_type: UINT. The function returns the value of the specified field if it is set in the dmFields member of the DEVMODEW structure. If the specified field is not set in dmFields, the function returns 0.

function.name: is_detached_mode
function.description: This function checks if the given mode is in detached mode by checking certain properties of the mode.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: This parameter represents the mode that is to be checked if it is in detached mode.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the mode is in detached mode, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: write_source_mode
function.description: This function writes the source mode to the registry. It first checks the index and converts it to a string representation. Then it sets the registry value based on the mode.

parameters.name: hkey
parameters.description: A handle to an open registry key.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: An index that represents the source mode. It can be ENUM_CURRENT_SETTINGS, ENUM_REGISTRY_SETTINGS, or WINE_ENUM_PHYSICAL_SETTINGS.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: A pointer to a DEVMODEW structure that contains information about the new settings for the source mode.

function.return_type: BOOL. Returns TRUE if the function successfully writes the source mode to the registry. Otherwise, it returns FALSE.

function.name: read_source_mode
function.description: This function reads the source mode from the registry, based on the provided index. It asserts that the index is one of the predefined constants, assigns a key based on the index, queries the registry for the key, and copies the result into the mode's dmFields.

parameters.name: hkey
parameters.description: A handle to an open registry key.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: An index that determines the source mode to be read. It should be one of the predefined constants: ENUM_CURRENT_SETTINGS, ENUM_REGISTRY_SETTINGS, or WINE_ENUM_PHYSICAL_SETTINGS.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: A pointer to a DEVMODEW structure that will receive the source mode data.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully reads the source mode and copies it into the mode's dmFields. Otherwise, it returns FALSE.

function.name: source_get_registry_settings
function.description: This function retrieves the registry settings for a given source and mode. It uses a mutex to ensure thread safety during the operation.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Pointer to the source structure from which registry settings are to be retrieved.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Pointer to the DEVMODEW structure where the retrieved registry settings will be stored.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the operation of retrieving registry settings was successful or not.

function.name: source_set_registry_settings
function.description: This function sets the registry settings for a given source and mode. It first obtains a mutex for the display device initialization, then attempts to open a registry key with the source's path. If successful, it writes the source mode to the registry and closes the key. Finally, it releases the mutex and returns the result of the operation.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Pointer to the source structure whose registry settings are to be set

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Pointer to the DEVMODEW structure that contains the new settings for the source

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the operation of setting the registry settings was successful or not

function.name: source_get_current_settings
function.description: This function copies the current settings from a source structure to a DEVMODEW structure and sets the bits per pixel if the source depth is non-zero.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Pointer to the source structure from which the current settings are copied

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Pointer to the DEVMODEW structure where the current settings are to be copied

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE indicating the operation was successful

function.name: source_set_current_settings
function.description: This function sets the current settings for a given source using a specified mode. It uses a mutex to ensure thread safety and writes the mode to a registry key. If successful, it also sets a registry value.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the source structure for which the settings are to be set.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the DEVMODEW structure that contains the mode settings to be set for the source.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function was successful in setting the current settings for the source. Returns TRUE if successful, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: mode_compare
function.description: This function compares two DEVMODEW structures, primarily used for sorting. It compares various fields in a specific order: depth, width, height, frequency, orientation, interlaced, and stretched.

parameters.name: p1
parameters.description: Pointer to the first DEVMODEW structure to be compared.

parameters.name: p2
parameters.description: Pointer to the second DEVMODEW structure to be compared.

function.return_type: int, represents the result of the comparison. If the return value is less than 0, the first structure is less than the second structure. If the return value is 0, the structures are equal. If the return value is greater than 0, the first structure is greater than the second structure.

function.name: query_reg_subkey_value
function.description: This function queries a registry subkey value.

parameters.name: hkey
parameters.description: Handle to an open registry key.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the subkey to query.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Pointer to a buffer that receives the key value information.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Size of the buffer pointed to by the value parameter.

function.return_type: unsigned int representing the size of the registry value data. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

function.name: read_source_from_registry
function.description: This function reads source information from the registry. It retrieves various properties of the source such as StateFlags, Dpi, Depth, ModeCount, Modes, current and physical display modes, and GPUID.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Index of the video device

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Pointer to the source structure to be filled with data from the registry

parameters.name: gpu_path
parameters.description: Pointer to a character array to be filled with the GPUID from the registry

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully reads the source information from the registry, otherwise returns FALSE

function.name: read_monitor_from_registry
function.description: This function reads monitor information from the registry. It retrieves the output ID, rc_work, and EDID of the monitor. If any of these operations fail, it returns FALSE. Otherwise, it returns TRUE.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: A pointer to a monitor structure where the retrieved information will be stored.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function was successful in reading the monitor information from the registry. Returns TRUE if successful, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: read_source_monitor_path
function.description: This function reads the source monitor path from the registry using the provided key and index, and stores it in the provided path buffer.

parameters.name: hkey
parameters.description: The registry key to read from.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The index of the monitor to read the path for.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The buffer to store the read path in.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the path was successfully read and stored, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: reg_empty_key
function.description: This function is used to empty a registry key. It first enumerates all subkeys of the given key and deletes them. Then it enumerates all values of the key and deletes them. If the provided key is not the root, it closes the key handle.

parameters.name: root
parameters.description: This is a handle to an open registry key. This handle is returned by the RegCreateKeyEx, RegOpenKeyEx, or RegConnectRegistry function. It can also be one of the following predefined keys: HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT, HKEY_CURRENT_USER, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, HKEY_USERS, HKEY_CURRENT_CONFIG.

parameters.name: key_name
parameters.description: This is the name of the subkey to be emptied. If this parameter is NULL, the function empties the key represented by the root parameter.

function.return_type: void, meaning it does not return a value

function.name: clear_display_devices
function.description: This function clears all display devices by releasing all monitors, sources, and gpus from their respective lists.

parameters.name: void
parameters.description: This function does not take any parameters.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: prepare_devices
function.description: This function prepares devices by clearing display devices, deleting monitors and sources, cleaning GPUs, and marking GPU GUIDs as not present. It interacts with the registry to perform these operations.

parameters.name: void
parameters.description: This function does not take any parameters

function.return_type: void, this function does not return any value

function.name: cleanup_devices
function.description: This function cleans up devices by enumerating through the registry keys, checking if the device is present and deleting the registry tree if the device is not present.

parameters.name: void
parameters.description: This function does not take any parameters.

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return any value.

function.name: uuid_create
function.description: This function generates a unique identifier (UUID) by querying system interrupt information and copying it into the provided GUID structure. It then modifies certain bits of the Data3 and Data4 fields to conform to the UUID specification.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: A pointer to a GUID structure where the generated UUID will be stored.

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return a value but instead modifies the GUID structure pointed to by the 'uuid' parameter.

function.name: format_date
function.description: This function formats a given time into a date string (year-month-day) and stores it in a buffer.

parameters.name: bufferW
parameters.description: A pointer to a wide character buffer where the formatted date string will be stored.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: The time value to be formatted into a date string.

function.return_type: unsigned int, represents the length of the formatted date string stored in the buffer.

function.name: link_device
function.description: This function creates a link for a device in the registry. It first formats the class and instance into a buffer, then creates a registry key with this buffer. It sets the 'DeviceInstance' value of this key to the instance. It then creates a subkey and sets the 'SymbolicLink' value to a formatted string of the instance and class. If a 'Control' subkey can be created, it sets a 'linked' value to 1.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: The instance of the device to be linked

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: The class of the device to be linked

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return any value

function.name: read_gpu_from_registry
function.description: This function reads GPU information from the system registry, including the GPU's index, name, LUID, GUID, and Vulkan UUID.

parameters.name: gpu
parameters.description: A pointer to a GPU structure where the read information will be stored.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully reads the GPU information from the registry, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: driver_vendor_to_version
function.description: This function returns the version number of the driver based on the vendor ID provided.

parameters.name: vendor
parameters.description: This parameter represents the vendor ID of the driver.

function.return_type: char, represents the version number of the driver as a string.

function.name: driver_vendor_to_name
function.description: This function takes a vendor ID as input and returns the corresponding vendor name as a string.

parameters.name: vendor
parameters.description: This parameter is used to specify the vendor ID.

function.return_type: char: This represents the name of the vendor corresponding to the input vendor ID.

function.name: write_gpu_to_registry
function.description: This function writes GPU information to the system registry.

parameters.name: gpu
parameters.description: Pointer to a GPU structure that contains information about the GPU.

parameters.name: pci
parameters.description: Pointer to a PCI ID structure that contains information about the PCI device.

parameters.name: memory_size
parameters.description: The size of the GPU memory.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the operation is successful, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: find_vulkan_gpu_from_uuid
function.description: This function searches for a Vulkan GPU using a given UUID in the device manager context. If the UUID is not found or is null, the function returns null.

parameters.name: ctx
parameters.description: This is the device manager context where the function searches for the Vulkan GPU.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: This is the UUID of the Vulkan GPU that the function is trying to find.

function.return_type: struct vulkan_gpu * - This represents a pointer to the Vulkan GPU structure that matches the given UUID. If no match is found, the function returns NULL.

function.name: find_vulkan_gpu_from_pci_id
function.description: This function searches for a Vulkan GPU in the device manager context using a given PCI ID. It iterates over each entry in the list of Vulkan GPUs in the context. If it finds a GPU with a matching vendor and device ID, it returns that GPU. If no matching GPU is found, it returns NULL.

parameters.name: ctx
parameters.description: This is the device manager context in which the function will search for the Vulkan GPU.

parameters.name: pci_id
parameters.description: This is the PCI ID that the function will use to search for the matching Vulkan GPU.

function.return_type: struct vulkan_gpu * - This is a pointer to the Vulkan GPU that matches the given PCI ID. If no matching GPU is found, the function returns NULL.

function.name: add_gpu
function.description: This function is used to add a GPU to the device manager context. It performs several operations such as creating keys in the registry, allocating memory for the GPU, and writing the GPU to the registry.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the GPU to be added.

parameters.name: pci_id
parameters.description: The PCI ID of the GPU to be added.

parameters.name: vulkan_uuid
parameters.description: The Vulkan UUID of the GPU to be added.

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: A pointer to the device manager context.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: write_source_to_registry
function.description: This function writes the source information to the system registry. It creates registry keys and sets their values based on the source and gpu data. It also handles the creation of symbolic links in the registry.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: This parameter is a pointer to the source structure that contains the information to be written to the registry.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully writes the source information to the registry, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: add_source
function.description: This function adds a source to a device manager context. It handles the allocation and initialization of the source structure, and writes the source to the registry. If the source is successfully written to the registry, it is added to the list of sources and the source count is incremented.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the source to be added.

parameters.name: state_flags
parameters.description: The state flags of the source.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The dpi of the source.

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: A pointer to the device manager context.

function.return_type: void

function.name: write_monitor_to_registry
function.description: This function writes monitor information to the registry. It creates and sets values for various registry keys related to the monitor. If any operation fails, it returns FALSE, otherwise it returns TRUE.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: Pointer to a monitor structure containing monitor information

parameters.name: edid
parameters.description: Pointer to a BYTE array representing the Extended Display Identification Data (EDID) of the monitor

parameters.name: edid_len
parameters.description: Length of the EDID data

function.return_type: BOOL, where TRUE indicates that the function executed successfully and FALSE indicates that it failed

function.name: add_monitor
function.description: This function adds a monitor to the device manager context. It initializes the monitor structure, gets monitor info from EDID, sets the registry value, and writes the monitor to the registry. If successful, it increments the monitor count in both the source and the context.

parameters.name: gdi_monitor
parameters.description: This is a pointer to a gdi_monitor structure that contains information about the monitor to be added.

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the device manager context where the monitor will be added.

function.return_type: void, meaning it does not return a value.

function.name: add_screen_size
function.description: This function adds a new screen size to an array of sizes if it does not already exist in the array.

parameters.name: sizes
parameters.description: This is a pointer to an array of SIZE structures representing different screen sizes.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: This is the number of elements in the 'sizes' array.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: This is the new screen size to be added to the 'sizes' array.

function.return_type: UINT, represents whether the new size was added to the array (1) or not (0).

function.name: add_virtual_mode
function.description: This function adds a virtual mode to the modes array at the index specified by count.

parameters.name: modes
parameters.description: Pointer to an array of DEVMODEW structures representing different modes.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Index at which the new mode should be added in the modes array.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Pointer to the DEVMODEW structure representing the mode to be added.

function.return_type: UINT, represents a success value. The function returns 1 after successfully adding the mode.

function.name: get_screen_sizes
function.description: This function is used to get the screen sizes. It calculates the maximum width and height, allocates memory for the sizes, and then adds the sizes to the allocated memory. It also checks if the sizes are within the maximum size. If not, it skips them. It returns the sizes.

parameters.name: maximum
parameters.description: Pointer to the maximum device mode

parameters.name: modes
parameters.description: Pointer to the device modes

parameters.name: modes_count
parameters.description: Count of the device modes

parameters.name: sizes_count
parameters.description: Pointer to the count of sizes

function.return_type: SIZE. It represents the sizes of the screens.

function.name: get_virtual_modes
function.description: This function generates a list of virtual display modes based on the initial, maximum and host modes provided. It checks the ratio of dmPelsWidth to dmPelsHeight to determine the orientation of the initial display mode. It then iterates over different depths and frequencies to generate the modes. The function also checks if the generated mode exceeds the maximum mode or matches the initial mode, in which case it skips adding the mode.

parameters.name: initial
parameters.description: Pointer to the initial display mode

parameters.name: maximum
parameters.description: Pointer to the maximum display mode

parameters.name: host_modes
parameters.description: Pointer to the host display modes

parameters.name: host_modes_count
parameters.description: Count of the host display modes

parameters.name: modes_count
parameters.description: Pointer to store the count of generated virtual modes

function.return_type: DEVMODEW *, represents a pointer to the generated virtual display modes

function.name: add_modes
function.description: This function manages device modes, handling different scenarios such as emulation, detachment, and registry settings. It also sets registry values and frees up memory.

parameters.name: current
parameters.description: Pointer to the current device mode

parameters.name: host_modes_count
parameters.description: Count of host modes

parameters.name: host_modes
parameters.description: Pointer to the host modes

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: Pointer to the device manager context

function.return_type: void, this function does not return any value

function.name: release_display_manager_ctx
function.description: This function releases the display manager context by releasing the mutex, cleaning up devices if there are any GPUs, and freeing up Vulkan GPUs if there are any in the list.

parameters.name: ctx
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the device manager context that needs to be released.

function.return_type: void, meaning it does not return anything.

function.name: is_monitor_active
function.description: This function checks if a monitor is active by checking its source and current settings.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the monitor structure that needs to be checked.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the monitor is active, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: is_monitor_primary
function.description: This function checks if the given monitor is the primary device.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: Pointer to the monitor structure to be checked.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the monitor is the primary device, otherwise FALSE.

function.name: monitor_virt_to_raw_ratio
function.description: This function calculates the ratio between the virtual and raw dimensions of a monitor's source. The ratio is determined based on the comparison of the product of the physical width and current height with the product of the physical height and current width of the source. The results are stored in the parameters num and den.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: A pointer to the monitor structure whose source's dimensions are to be used for the ratio calculation

parameters.name: num
parameters.description: A pointer to an unsigned integer where the numerator of the ratio will be stored

parameters.name: den
parameters.description: A pointer to an unsigned integer where the denominator of the ratio will be stored

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return any value but modifies the values of the parameters passed to it

function.name: monitor_get_dpi
function.description: This function calculates the DPI (dots per inch) for a given monitor and type, and updates the dpi_x and dpi_y values. It returns the minimum of dpi_x and dpi_y.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: Pointer to the monitor structure for which DPI is to be calculated

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of DPI to be calculated

parameters.name: dpi_x
parameters.description: Pointer to store the calculated DPI in x direction

parameters.name: dpi_y
parameters.description: Pointer to store the calculated DPI in y direction

function.return_type: UINT, represents the minimum of dpi_x and dpi_y

function.name: map_monitor_rect
function.description: This function maps a rectangle from one DPI type to another for a given monitor. If the monitor has a source, it calculates the mapping using the current and physical modes of the source. Otherwise, it uses the monitor's DPI for the given types.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: The monitor for which the rectangle is being mapped.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: The rectangle to be mapped.

parameters.name: dpi_from
parameters.description: The DPI type from which the rectangle is being mapped.

parameters.name: type_from
parameters.description: The DPI type from which the rectangle is being mapped.

parameters.name: dpi_to
parameters.description: The DPI type to which the rectangle is being mapped.

parameters.name: type_to
parameters.description: The DPI type to which the rectangle is being mapped.

function.return_type: RECT, the mapped rectangle.

function.name: monitor_get_rect
function.description: This function retrieves the rectangle of a monitor based on the given DPI and DPI type. It also handles cases where the monitor is a virtual monitor or not attached to the desktop.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: A pointer to the monitor structure to get the rectangle from.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The DPI (dots per inch) to use for the rectangle calculation.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The type of DPI to use for the rectangle calculation.

function.return_type: RECT, which represents the calculated rectangle of the monitor.

function.name: monitor_get_info
function.description: This function retrieves information about a specified monitor and updates a MONITORINFO structure or a MONITORINFOEX structure with data.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: Pointer to the monitor structure to get information from.

parameters.name: info
parameters.description: Pointer to a MONITORINFO structure that receives information about the specified display monitor.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The DPI setting for the monitor.

function.return_type: void

function.name: set_winstation_monitors
function.description: This function sets the monitor information for a window station. It iterates over the list of monitors, checks their status and updates their information. It then sends this information to the server.

parameters.name: increment
parameters.description: This parameter is used to increment the count of monitors in the server request.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything

function.name: enum_device_keys
function.description: This function enumerates device keys in the registry. It opens a root key, then iterates over its subkeys (devices). For each device, it iterates over its subkeys (instances), checks if the 'ClassGUID' value matches the provided class, and if so, it calls the callback with the instance path.

parameters.name: root
parameters.description: This is the root key path in the registry.

parameters.name: classW
parameters.description: This is the class GUID to match against.

parameters.name: class_size
parameters.description: This is the size of the class GUID.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: This is a callback function that is called with the path of each matching instance.

function.return_type: void

function.name: enum_gpus
function.description: This function enumerates GPUs by allocating memory for a new GPU, setting its reference count to 1, copying the provided path into the GPU's path, and adding the GPU to the tail of a list of GPUs.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: This parameter is used to specify the path of the GPU.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value.

function.name: find_gpu_from_path
function.description: This function searches for a GPU structure in a list of GPUs using a given path. If the GPU is found, it is acquired and returned. If not, an error message is printed and NULL is returned.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: This is the path used to find the GPU in the list of GPUs.

function.return_type: struct gpu *; this represents the GPU found at the given path. If no GPU is found, NULL is returned.

function.name: enum_monitors
function.description: This function allocates memory for a new monitor structure, sets its refcount to 1, copies the provided path into the monitor's path, and adds the monitor to the end of a list of monitors.

parameters.name: path

function.name: add_virtual_source

parameters.name: void
parameters.description: This function does not take any parameters

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything

parameters.name: force

function.name: get_display_dc

parameters.description: This function does not take any parameters.

function.name: release_display_dc
function.description: This function releases the display device context by unlocking the mutex.

parameters.name: hdc

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

parameters.description: A handle to the window for which the DPI is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: raw_dpi
parameters.description: A pointer to a UINT where the raw DPI value will be stored.

parameters.name: void
parameters.description: This function does not take any parameters.

function.return_type: DWORD, representing the process layout or 0 if the process layout equals to ~0u

function.return_type: UINT, represents the system's DPI if the system is DPI aware, otherwise returns the default screen DPI

If the context is valid, it sets the DPI context of the thread to the provided context, or to 0 if the NTUSER_DPI_CONTEXT_FLAG_PROCESS flag is set in the context. The function returns the previous DPI context of the thread.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: The DPI awareness context to set for the current thread.

function.return_type: UINT, represents the previous DPI context of the thread.

parameters.description: The rectangle to be mapped.

parameters.description: The handle to the region to be mapped.

parameters.name: dpi_from
parameters.description: The DPI of the original region.

parameters.description: The DPI to which the region should be mapped.

parameters.description: A physical point that needs to be converted to window DPI.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the DPI is to be retrieved.

function.description: This function opens an adapter from a GDI display name. It initializes a unicode string with the device name, finds the source of the device, and if successful, updates the adapter and LUID in the descriptor. It also releases the source before returning the status.

parameters.name: desc
parameters.description: This is a pointer to a descriptor that contains the GDI display name. It is used to open the adapter and retrieve the LUID. The function also updates this descriptor with the adapter handle, LUID, and VidPnSourceId.

function.return_type: NTSTATUS, which represents the status of the operation. If successful, the function returns STATUS_SUCCESS. If the device name is not found or the source of the device cannot be found, the function returns STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL.

function.name: NtUserEnumDisplayDevices
function.description: This function enumerates display devices in the system, providing information about each device.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Pointer to a UNICODE_STRING that specifies the device name.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Specifies the index of the device in the array of devices.

parameters.name: info
parameters.description: Pointer to a DISPLAY_DEVICEW structure that receives information about the display device.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Specifies flags that modify the function's behavior.

function.return_type: NTSTATUS - Returns STATUS_SUCCESS if the function successfully found the display device, otherwise returns STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL.

function.name: _CDS_flags
function.description: This function generates a string representation of the flags set in the 'fields' parameter. It uses a buffer to store the string and returns a pointer to this string.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: This parameter represents the flags that need to be converted to a string.

function.return_type: char: This is a pointer to the string representation of the flags.

function.name: _DM_fields
function.description: This function generates a string representation of various display settings fields. It uses a buffer to concatenate the fields and returns the final string.
function.return_type: char: Returns a string representation of the display settings fields

function.name: trace_devmode
function.description: This function traces the properties of a DEVMODEW structure, such as dmFields, dmBitsPerPel, dmPelsWidth, dmPelsHeight, dmDisplayFrequency, dmPosition, dmDisplayFlags, and dmDisplayOrientation.

parameters.name: devmode
parameters.description: A pointer to a DEVMODEW structure whose properties are to be traced.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value

function.name: find_display_mode
function.description: This function iterates over a list of display modes and returns the one that matches the provided devmode. If no matching mode is found, it returns NULL. If the devmode is in detached mode, the function returns the devmode itself.

parameters.name: modes
parameters.description: Pointer to the first element in the list of display modes to search.

parameters.name: devmode
parameters.description: Pointer to the display mode that the function is trying to find in the list.

function.return_type: DEVMODEW *. It represents the display mode that matches the provided devmode. If no matching mode is found, it returns NULL.

function.name: source_get_full_mode
function.description: This function gets the full mode of a source. It checks the devmode and if it's valid, it copies it to full_mode. If it's not valid, it retrieves the settings from the registry. It also checks if the resolution is specified and if not, it gets the current settings. Finally, it finds the display mode and if it's different from the full_mode, it updates the full_mode with the display mode.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Pointer to the source structure

parameters.name: devmode
parameters.description: Pointer to the DEVMODEW structure that represents the device mode

parameters.name: full_mode
parameters.description: Pointer to the DEVMODEW structure that will hold the full mode

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the source mode is found, otherwise returns FALSE

function.name: get_display_settings
function.description: This function retrieves the display settings for a given source. If a DEVMODEW structure is provided, it copies the display settings from it. Otherwise, it retrieves the settings from the registry or the current settings of the source. The function returns a pointer to an array of DEVMODEW structures, each representing the display settings of a source.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The target source for which the display settings are to be retrieved.

parameters.name: devmode
parameters.description: A pointer to a DEVMODEW structure from which to copy the display settings. If this parameter is NULL, the function retrieves the settings from the registry or the current settings of the source.

function.return_type: DEVMODEW*. Returns a pointer to an array of DEVMODEW structures, each representing the display settings of a source. If the function fails to allocate memory for the array, or if it fails to retrieve the settings, it returns NULL.

function.name: offset_length
function.description: Calculates the square of the x and y coordinates of the given point and returns their sum

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: A point in 2D space

function.return_type: INT, represents the sum of the squares of the x and y coordinates of the given point

function.name: set_rect_from_devmode
function.description: This function sets the values of a rectangle using the position and dimensions from a DEVMODEW structure.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: This is a pointer to a RECT structure that will be set based on the mode parameter.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: This is a pointer to a DEVMODEW structure that contains the position and dimensions to set the rect parameter.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value

function.name: overlap_placed_displays
function.description: This function checks if any of the displays overlap with the given rectangle.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: This parameter is a pointer to a RECT structure that represents the rectangle to check for overlap.

parameters.name: displays
parameters.description: This parameter is a pointer to a DEVMODEW structure that represents the display settings.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if any of the displays overlap with the given rectangle, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: get_placement_offset
function.description: This function calculates the minimum offset needed to place a display in a multi-display setup without overlapping other displays.

parameters.name: displays
parameters.description: Pointer to the first element of an array of DEVMODEW structures representing the current display settings.

parameters.name: placing
parameters.description: Pointer to a DEVMODEW structure representing the display settings of the display to be placed.

function.return_type: POINT structure representing the minimum offset needed to place the display without overlap.

function.name: place_all_displays
function.description: This function adjusts the positions of all displays to ensure there is no extra space between them and no overlapping. It also sets the primary display based on the provided name.

parameters.name: displays
parameters.description: A pointer to the DEVMODEW structure that represents the display settings.

parameters.name: primary_name
parameters.description: A pointer to the wide-character string that represents the name of the primary display.

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return anything but modifies the display settings in place.

function.name: all_detached_settings
function.description: This function checks if all display settings are detached by iterating through each DEVMODEW structure in the 'displays' pointer until it encounters a structure with a dmSize of zero. If it finds a display setting that is not detached, it returns FALSE. If all display settings are detached, it returns TRUE.

parameters.name: displays
parameters.description: This is a pointer to a DEVMODEW structure that represents the display settings.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether all display settings are detached (TRUE) or not (FALSE)

function.name: get_primary_source_mode
function.description: This function gets the current settings of the primary source and releases the source after getting the settings.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Pointer to a DEVMODEW structure that will receive the current settings of the primary source.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the current settings of the primary source were successfully retrieved, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: display_mode_changed
function.description: This function updates the display cache, gets the primary source current display settings, and sends a message or broadcasts a message depending on the 'broadcast' parameter. If an application changed the display settings, it also posts a clip_fullscreen_window request to the foreground window.

parameters.name: broadcast
parameters.description: This parameter determines whether the function should send a message to a single window or broadcast a message to all windows.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return any value

function.name: apply_display_settings
function.description: This function applies the display settings to a target source. It locks the display devices, gets the display settings, checks if all settings are detached, finds the primary source, places all displays, changes the display settings, unlocks the display devices, frees the displays, and returns the result.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The target source to which the display settings are applied.

parameters.name: devmode
parameters.description: The device mode to be used.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the display settings are applied.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: The options for changing the display settings.

parameters.name: lparam
parameters.description: Additional data for the function.

function.return_type: LONG, represents the result of applying the display settings. It can be DISP_CHANGE_SUCCESSFUL, DISP_CHANGE_FAILED, or other values.

function.name: NtUserChangeDisplaySettings
function.description: This function is used to change the display settings of a device. It checks the validity of the parameters, retrieves the full mode of the source, updates the registry settings if necessary, applies the display settings, and releases the source.

parameters.name: devname
parameters.description: Pointer to the name of the device whose display settings are to be changed.

parameters.name: devmode
parameters.description: Pointer to a DEVMODEW structure that contains the new graphics mode.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window that will be updated after the display settings change.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Indicates how the graphics mode should be changed.

parameters.name: lparam
parameters.description: Additional parameters for the function.

function.return_type: LONG. Returns DISP_CHANGE_SUCCESSFUL if the function succeeds. Otherwise, it returns an error code such as DISP_CHANGE_BADPARAM, DISP_CHANGE_BADMODE, DISP_CHANGE_NOTUPDATED.

function.name: source_enum_display_settings
function.description: This function enumerates the display settings of a given source. It checks for specific flags and modes and copies the display settings to the devmode parameter if the conditions are met.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Pointer to the source structure whose display settings are to be enumerated.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Index of the display setting to be enumerated.

parameters.name: devmode
parameters.description: Pointer to a DEVMODEW structure that will receive the display settings.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags that determine the behavior of the function.

function.return_type: BOOL. Returns TRUE if the function successfully enumerates the display settings. Returns FALSE if it fails to do so.

function.name: NtUserEnumDisplaySettings
function.description: This function is used to enumerate the display settings.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Pointer to a unicode string representing the device.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Index of the display setting to be enumerated.

parameters.name: devmode
parameters.description: Pointer to a DEVMODEW structure that will receive the display settings.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to be used for the enumeration.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully enumerates the display settings, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: active_unique_monitor_count
function.description: This function counts the number of unique active monitors that are not clones.
function.return_type: unsigned int representing the count of unique active monitors

function.name: get_display_depth
function.description: This function retrieves the display depth of a given source. If the source is not found or cannot be locked, it defaults to a depth of 32.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: This is a pointer to a UNICODE_STRING that represents the name of the source to find.

function.return_type: INT, represents the display depth of the source. If the source is not found or cannot be locked, it returns 32.

function.name: should_enumerate_monitor
function.description: This function checks if a monitor should be enumerated based on its activity status, whether it is a clone, and its position relative to a given origin and limit. It also modifies the provided rectangle to represent the monitor's rectangle offset by the given origin.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: Pointer to the monitor to check.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Pointer to the origin point used for offsetting the monitor's rectangle.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Pointer to the rectangle representing the limit for enumeration.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a rectangle that will be set to represent the monitor's rectangle offset by the origin.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the monitor should be enumerated, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: NtUserEnumDisplayMonitors
function.description: This function enumerates display monitors. It first enumerates primary monitors, then non-primary monitors. It also handles the locking and unlocking of display devices.

parameters.name: hdc
parameters.description: Handle to a device context.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that specifies a clipping rectangle.

parameters.name: proc
parameters.description: A pointer to a callback function that is called for each display monitor.

parameters.name: lparam
parameters.description: An application-defined data passed to the callback function.

function.return_type: BOOL. Returns TRUE if the function successfully enumerates the display monitors, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: get_monitor_info
function.description: This function retrieves information about a display monitor. It checks the size of the MONITORINFO structure, locks the display devices, gets the monitor from the handle, retrieves the monitor information, unlocks the display devices, and sets the last Win32 error if the handle is invalid.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: Handle to the display monitor.

parameters.name: info
parameters.description: Pointer to a MONITORINFO structure that receives information about the specified display monitor.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: Dots per inch.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function succeeds, or FALSE otherwise.

function.name: monitor_from_rect
function.description: This function retrieves a handle to the display monitor that has the largest area of intersection with a specified rectangle, based on certain flags and dpi.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: A pointer to the rectangle of interest.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags that determine the function's behavior.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The DPI setting for the monitor.

function.return_type: HMONITOR, which represents a handle to the display monitor. Returns 0 if the function fails.

function.name: monitor_info_from_rect
function.description: This function retrieves monitor information for a given rectangle and DPI, locks the display devices, gets the monitor from the rectangle, retrieves the monitor information, and then unlocks the display devices.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: This parameter represents the rectangle for which the monitor information is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: This parameter represents the DPI (Dots Per Inch) for the monitor.

function.return_type: MONITORINFO, which represents the information about the monitor.

function.name: monitor_dpi_from_rect
function.description: This function retrieves the DPI (dots per inch) of a monitor based on a given rectangle. It also updates the raw DPI value.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: The rectangle based on which the monitor is identified

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The DPI value

parameters.name: raw_dpi
parameters.description: Pointer to a UINT to store the raw DPI value

function.return_type: UINT, represents the DPI of the monitor associated with the given rectangle

function.name: monitor_from_window
function.description: This function retrieves a handle to the display monitor that has the largest area of intersection with the bounding rectangle of a specified window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Determines the function's return value if the window does not intersect any display monitor.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The DPI value for the window.

function.return_type: HMONITOR, a handle to the display monitor. If the window does not intersect any display monitor and the function was not able to retrieve a monitor handle, it returns NULL.

function.name: monitor_info_from_window
function.description: This function retrieves monitor information for a specific window based on the provided flags.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which monitor information is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags that determine the function's behavior.

function.return_type: MONITORINFO structure that contains information about the display monitor.

function.name: NtUserGetSystemDpiForProcess
function.description: This function returns the system DPI for the specified process. If the process is not the current one, it returns 0.

parameters.name: process
parameters.description: This parameter represents the handle to the process for which the system DPI is to be obtained.

function.return_type: ULONG. It represents the system DPI for the specified process. If the process is not the current one, it returns 0.

function.name: NtUserGetDpiForMonitor
function.description: This function retrieves the dots per inch (dpi) value for a specified monitor based on the type of dpi awareness the current process is running under. It also handles error cases and sets appropriate error codes.

parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: Handle to the monitor for which the dpi value is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Specifies the type of dpi awareness context.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Pointer to a variable that receives the horizontal dpi value for the specified monitor.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Pointer to a variable that receives the vertical dpi value for the specified monitor.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully retrieves the dpi value for the specified monitor, otherwise returns FALSE and sets an error code.

function.name: NtUserLogicalToPerMonitorDPIPhysicalPoint
function.description: This function converts a logical point to a physical point based on the DPI of the monitor the window is currently displayed on. It also checks whether the point is within the window rectangle.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window that the point is relative to.

parameters.name: pt
parameters.description: Pointer to the POINT structure that specifies the logical coordinates to be converted.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully converts the point and the point is within the window rectangle. Otherwise, it returns FALSE.

function.name: NtUserPerMonitorDPIPhysicalToLogicalPoint
function.description: This function converts a point from physical coordinates to logical coordinates based on the DPI of the monitor the window is on.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window that the point is in.

parameters.name: pt
parameters.description: Pointer to the POINT structure that specifies the physical coordinates to be converted.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the conversion is successful, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: set_server_keyboard_repeat
function.description: This function is used to set the keyboard repeat rate on the server side.

parameters.name: enable
parameters.description: This parameter is used to enable or disable the keyboard repeat feature.

parameters.name: delay
parameters.description: This parameter is used to set the delay before the keyboard repeat starts.

parameters.name: speed
parameters.description: This parameter is used to set the speed of the keyboard repeat.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the keyboard repeat setting was successfully updated or not.

function.name: get_base_keys
function.description: This function retrieves or creates base and volatile keys in the registry based on the provided index. If the keys do not exist, they are created using the reg_create_ascii_key function. The keys are then stored in static arrays for future use.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: This parameter is used to specify the index of the key in the base_keys and volatile_keys arrays.

parameters.name: base_key
parameters.description: This is a pointer to a HKEY variable where the function will store the base key retrieved or created.

parameters.name: volatile_key
parameters.description: This is a pointer to a HKEY variable where the function will store the volatile key retrieved or created.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully retrieves or creates the keys, and FALSE if it fails to create the keys.

function.name: load_entry
function.description: This function loads an entry from the system registry into a provided buffer, ensuring that the data is null-terminated if it is a string. It also sets the 'loaded' flag on the entry to TRUE.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the system parameter entry to be loaded

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Pointer to the buffer where the loaded data will be stored

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The size of the buffer pointed to by 'data'

function.return_type: DWORD, represents the number of bytes loaded into the buffer. If the function fails, it returns FALSE

function.name: save_entry
function.description: This function saves an entry into the system registry. It converts the entry name to unicode, gets the base keys, sets the registry value, and deletes the volatile key. If the entry has a mirror, it also sets the mirror value. If the SPIF_UPDATEINIFILE flag is not set, it only sets the volatile key value.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the system parameter entry to be saved

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Pointer to the data to be saved

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Size of the data to be saved

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of the data to be saved

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to control the save operation

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the operation is successful, FALSE otherwise

function.name: save_entry_string
function.description: This function saves an entry string into the system parameter entry.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the system parameter entry

parameters.name: str
parameters.description: String to be saved

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to control the save operation

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the save operation was successful or not

function.name: init_entry
function.description: This function initializes a system parameter entry by querying its value key, setting its registry value, and marking it as loaded. It also handles mirror keys if present.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: A pointer to the system parameter entry to be initialized

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: A pointer to the data to be set in the registry value

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The size of the data to be set in the registry value

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The type of the data to be set in the registry value

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the initialization is successful, FALSE otherwise

function.name: init_entry_string
function.description: Initializes a system parameter entry with a string value

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the system parameter entry to be initialized

parameters.name: str
parameters.description: String to be used for initialization

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the initialization was successful or not

function.name: set_int_entry
function.description: This function converts an integer parameter to a string, converts that string to unicode, saves the unicode string into an entry, sets the integer parameter as the value of the entry, and marks the entry as loaded.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the entry where the integer parameter and its string representation will be stored

parameters.name: int_param
parameters.description: Integer parameter to be converted to string and stored in the entry

parameters.name: ptr_param
parameters.description: Pointer parameter, not used in the function

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to be passed when saving the string into the entry

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the string is successfully saved into the entry and the entry is marked as loaded, otherwise returns FALSE

function.name: init_int_entry
function.description: This function initializes an integer entry by converting it to a string and then to a unicode string, and finally initializes the entry string with the unicode string.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: This parameter is a pointer to a union of system parameters. The function uses the integer value from this union.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the initialization of the entry string was successful or not

function.name: get_uint_entry
function.description: This function loads an entry if it's not loaded, converts it to a long integer, and assigns it to a pointer. If the pointer is null, it returns false.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: pointer to the entry to get

parameters.name: int_param
parameters.description: an unsigned integer parameter

parameters.name: ptr_param
parameters.description: pointer to assign the entry value to

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: an unsigned integer parameter

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the operation is successful, FALSE otherwise

function.name: set_uint_entry
function.description: This function sets a UINT entry in a system parameter union. It converts the integer parameter to a string, converts that string to unicode, saves the unicode string into the entry header, and sets the UINT value in the entry. It also sets the loaded flag in the entry header to TRUE.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the system parameter entry to be set

parameters.name: int_param
parameters.description: Integer value to be set in the entry

parameters.name: ptr_param
parameters.description: Pointer parameter, not used in this function

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to be used when saving the entry string

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the entry string was saved successfully and the UINT value was set in the entry, otherwise returns FALSE

function.name: init_uint_entry
function.description: This function initializes a union sysparam_all_entry with a unsigned integer value, converts it to a string and stores it in the entry.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the union sysparam_all_entry that is to be initialized.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the initialization was successful or not.

function.name: get_twips_entry
function.description: This function retrieves the value of an entry in a system parameter structure, converts it from twips to pixels if it's negative, or maps it to the current DPI if it's positive, and stores the result in a provided pointer.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the system parameter entry to retrieve the value from.

parameters.name: int_param
parameters.description: An unsigned integer parameter, not used in the function.

parameters.name: ptr_param
parameters.description: Pointer to an integer where the result will be stored.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The current DPI (dots per inch) setting, used for conversion if the value is positive.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the operation is successful, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: set_twips_entry
function.description: This function sets the value of an entry after mapping it from system dpi if it's greater than 0, then calls the function set_int_entry with the processed value and other parameters.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the entry to be set

parameters.name: int_param
parameters.description: Integer parameter to be processed and set to the entry

parameters.name: ptr_param
parameters.description: Pointer parameter to be passed to the function set_int_entry

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to be passed to the function set_int_entry

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function set_int_entry executed successfully or not

function.name: get_bool_entry
function.description: This function loads a boolean entry from a system parameter, if it's not already loaded, and stores the value in a provided pointer.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the system parameter entry.

parameters.name: int_param
parameters.description: An unsigned integer parameter. However, it's not used in the function.

parameters.name: ptr_param
parameters.description: Pointer where the boolean value of the entry will be stored.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: An unsigned integer parameter. However, it's not used in the function.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the operation is successful, FALSE if the ptr_param is NULL.

function.name: set_bool_entry
function.description: This function sets a boolean entry in a system parameter union. It also saves the entry string and sets the loaded flag to true.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to a system parameter union where the boolean entry will be set.

parameters.name: int_param
parameters.description: Integer parameter that will be used to set the boolean value and the entry string.

parameters.name: ptr_param
parameters.description: Pointer parameter that is not used in this function.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags that will be passed to the save_entry_string function.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the entry string is successfully saved and the boolean value is set, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: init_bool_entry
function.description: This function initializes a boolean entry by converting the boolean value to a string and then initializing the entry string with this value.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the union sysparam_all_entry structure that needs to be initialized.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the initialization of the entry string was successful or not.

function.name: get_yesno_entry
function.description: This function loads an entry if it's not loaded, checks the value and sets it to the boolean value of the entry. If the pointer parameter is null, it returns false, otherwise it returns true.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the entry to get

parameters.name: int_param
parameters.description: An unsigned integer parameter

parameters.name: ptr_param
parameters.description: Pointer parameter to be checked and set

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: An unsigned integer parameter

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function executes successfully, otherwise returns FALSE

function.name: set_yesno_entry
function.description: This function sets a yes/no entry in a system parameter structure. It also sets the 'loaded' flag of the header to TRUE.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the system parameter entry to be set

parameters.name: int_param
parameters.description: Integer parameter used to determine the string to be saved in the entry

parameters.name: ptr_param
parameters.description: Unused parameter in the function

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags used when saving the string to the entry

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the string is successfully saved and the boolean value and 'loaded' flag are set, otherwise returns FALSE

function.name: init_yesno_entry
function.description: Initializes a yes/no entry by calling the init_entry_string function with the appropriate parameters.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the entry to be initialized.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the initialization was successful or not.

function.name: get_dword_entry
function.description: This function retrieves a DWORD entry from a system parameter union. If the entry is not loaded, it attempts to load it. The retrieved value is then stored in the memory location pointed to by ptr_param.

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to the system parameter union from which to retrieve the DWORD entry

parameters.name: int_param
parameters.description: An unsigned integer parameter. However, it is not used in the function body.
